# ferentin_mcp_local_server (Resource)

Local MCP server approval — a locally spawned (stdio) MCP server that managed devices run governed, through `ferentin-mcp`, instead of refusing it under `unapproved_mcp_action`.

Create one from **exactly one** of:

* `argv_template` (with `display_name`) — the command line the approval covers, where `*` matches exactly one argument: `["uv", "run", "--directory", "*", "okta-mcp-server"]` approves that server from any directory. Devices consult a template only for a command line that names no package.
* `catalog_slug` — a local MCP catalog entry, keyed on its package identities.

Either way the server is approved on creation, tenant-wide. Its tools still start unvetted; `local_mcp_risk_policy` on `ferentin_endpoint_policy_settings` decides what developers get from them.

Import manages the verdict of a server a device reported, too. Such a server cannot be deleted: destroying it leaves it, and its verdict, in place, with a warning.

~> The template is shipped **verbatim** in the signed policy bundle to every managed device. Put `*` where a credential or anything private would go.

## Import

```
terraform import ferentin_mcp_local_server.example <tenant_id>/<server_id>
```

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Approve a local (stdio) MCP server from the command line that runs it. `*`
# matches exactly one argument, so this covers okta-mcp-server from any
# checkout directory. The template ships verbatim to every managed device:
# put `*` where anything private would go.
resource "ferentin_mcp_local_server" "okta" {
  display_name  = "Okta MCP"
  argv_template = ["uv", "run", "--directory", "*", "okta-mcp-server"]
  reason        = "Approved for the identity team's runbooks"
}

# Approve a server from the local MCP catalog, keyed on its packages.
resource "ferentin_mcp_local_server" "playwright" {
  catalog_slug = "local-playwright"
}

# Block a server outright. Devices consult a template only for a command line
# that names no package, so a template suits a bare binary or a script; block
# a package with an endpoint MCP rule instead. A server a device reported can
# be imported to manage its verdict this way; destroying it leaves it in place.
resource "ferentin_mcp_local_server" "unvetted" {
  display_name  = "Unvetted scraper"
  argv_template = ["/opt/tools/scraper-mcp", "--stdio"]
  status        = "blocked"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `argv_template` (List of String) The command line the approval covers, as the client's config spells it (`argv[0]` included); `*` matches exactly one argument and every other token is compared literally. At least two tokens must be literal. Changing it updates the server in place. Leaving it out keeps the server's current template.
- `catalog_slug` (String) Slug of the local MCP catalog entry to add the server from, e.g. `local-playwright`. Changing it replaces the server.
- `display_name` (String) Name shown in the console. Required with `argv_template`; a catalog server takes its entry's. Changing it replaces the server.
- `reason` (String) Note recorded in the audit log with each write. Not read back.
- `status` (String) The verdict: `approved` (devices run it, governed), `blocked`, or `pending` (no decision: `unapproved_mcp_action` applies). A created server starts `approved`. Leaving it out keeps the current verdict.
- `tenant_id` (String)

### Read-Only

- `approvable` (Boolean) False when the command line is too long for a device to keep it released once approved.
- `approval_refused` (Boolean) True when the platform refuses to approve the server, for the reason in `approval_refused_reason`.
- `approval_refused_reason` (String)
- `argv_hash` (String)
- `declared_via` (String) `template`, `catalog`, or null for a server a device reported.
- `effective_status` (String) How admission treats the server now: `status`, except that a pending server covered by an approved one reads `approved`.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `kind` (String) `local` (spawned on a developer's machine) or `remote`.
- `last_modified_by` (String) Provenance of the most recent governance write. Divergence from `managed_by` is the drift signal.
- `managed_by` (String) Who created the server: `iac` for this provider, `console`, or `system` for one a device reported. Immutable.
- `managed_by_client_id` (String) OAuth2 `client_id` of the creator.
- `managed_by_module` (String) Module label the creator sent via `X-Ferentin-Managed-By-Module`.
- `packages` (List of String) Registry-qualified package identities the approval is keyed on, e.g. `npm:@acme/server`.
- `server_id` (String)
- `slug` (String)
- `steerable` (Boolean) Whether the approval reaches the fleet: the device bundle carries a match key for it (a template, packages, or an argv hash).
- `version` (Number) Optimistic-concurrency version, sent as `If-Match` on update and delete so a concurrent console edit is rejected with 412 rather than overwritten.
